To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
during early zebrafsh heart development, three different modes of myocardial migration can be observed: co-migration, subduction and migration independent of the endodermal convergence.
the endoderm undergoes three different phases of convergence during segmentation, and these phases are associated with different modes of myocardial migration.
during heart-tube development, the endoderm undergoes three distinct phases of convergence, and myocardial cells exhibit three distinct migration modes, all of which depend on S1pr signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of heart development, in particular, the role of the endodermal tissue in the formation of the heart.
the mechanisms that control heart development, and in particular how the movement of the myocardial cells is coordinated with the movement of adjacent endodermal and mesodermal cells.
the mechanisms that control endoderm and cardiac cell movements during early zebrafisch heart development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endodermal convergence is essential for heart tube formation and that the mechanism is dependent on the S1pr/Gα13 signaling cascade.
S1pr2-Gα13 signalling is essential for endoderm and mesodermal subduction during early heart development.
S1pr2 signalling controls three distinct phases of myocardial migration and that the three phases of myocardial cell movement rely on S1P2/Gα13-dependent endoderm convergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S1pr2-Galpha13 signalling is essential for the coordination of endodermal and myocardial cell movements during heart development.
S1pr2-mediated endoderm convergence is crucial for the subduction of the cardiac precursors, and thus for heart formation.
the S1pr/Gα13 signaling controls endoderm convergence that coordinates subduction of myocardial precursors and other ALPM cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endoderm convergence controls the migration and organization of the myocardial cells during heart tube formation.
the endoderm is essential for myocardial cell migration during heart formation.
endoderm convergence is essential for heart formation.
